methods.label: Compare the error with the correct result
methods.explanation:
The phrase “based on the correct answer” tells us to divide the error by the correct result. Let the original number be \(a>0\). The correct result is \(6a\), and the mistaken result is \(a/6\). Since the mistaken result is smaller, the error is \(6a-a/6\).

Its percentage of the correct result is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{6a-a/6}{6a}\cdot100\%
&=\frac{35}{36}\cdot100\%\\
&\approx97.22\%.
\end{aligned}
\]
The denominator is nonzero because \(a>0\). Rounding to the nearest whole percent gives \(97\%\), choice B.
